title.title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
title.subtitle: Claim: at $p = 3$ the classes $b_j$ survive exactly for $j = 0, 2, 3$, in stems 10, 106 and 322

plain: Which dimensions allow certain exotic twisted shapes? At the prime three, exactly three candidates survive

panels.caption: green: known to survive · red: dies · colour: newly claimed survivor

panels.axisLabel: stem of the mod-3 Adams spectral sequence

beats.text: Odd-primary Kervaire classes $b_j$: $b_0$ and $b_2$ survive, $b_1$ dies
The claim: $b_3$ survives too, and every $b_j$ with $j \ge 4$ dies
The new class in stem 322 is built from the known stem-106 class

steps: Send each class to a detector built from a symmetry of order nine
There, built-in 'deadlines' force classes past index 3 to die
So only indices 0, 2 and 3 survive; index 3 is built by hand

achievement.label: Kervaire invariant problem at the prime 3
achievement.context: Each detected by an element of exact order 3. At $p = 2$: Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel (2016)
achievement.note: 90 pages of spectral-sequence bookkeeping, not yet audited

verify.detail: Manuscript only: 90 pages, via $C_9$ acting on height-6 Morava E-theory
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the differentials

voice.text: Candidates b zero and b two survive. The claim settles all of the rest.
A detector sets deadlines: later classes must die, b three survives.
Claimed: only zero, two and three survive.

sources.quote: At p = 3, the standard odd-primary Kervaire classes b_j in the mod-3 Adams spectral sequence survive exactly for j in {0,2,3} (stems 10, 106, 322), each detected by an element of exact order 3; b_1 and all b_j, j >= 4, die.
at p = 3 the survival of b_0, b_2 was known and b_1 dies; higher indices open.
90 pages; proves a conjectured coefficient-action model
